name: Copper
description: Copper! The furnace becomes a smelter, and new ores are found.

name: Bronze
description: The Bronze Age, and the brewers and vintners of Sumer and Egypt: the Fermenter is unlocked.

name: Brass
description: Bronze and brass buy gold, silver ore, cinnabar and kohl from the traders.

name: Iron
description: The Iron Age. Distillation is invented, and the markets of antiquity open.

name: Glass
description: Glass vessels: you can now chill and crystallise in an ice bath.

name: Ethanol
description: Spirit of wine. The perfumers turn the still on the herb garden.

name: Acetic Acid
description: Vinegar keeps the harvest: the pantry and the apothecary's jars fill up.

name: Sulfuric Acid
description: Oil of vitriol. The alchemists' cabinet fills with strange salts.

name: Nitric Acid
description: Aqua fortis eats metal and stone; only glass can hold it. The Glass Flask is unlocked.

name: White phosphorus
description: Brand's phosphorus ends the age of alchemy. Coal, air and the mineral cabinets of the new chemists.

name: Silver Chloride
description: Horn silver darkens in the sun: light itself can drive chemistry.

name: Coke
description: Abraham Darby's coke (1709) burns hot enough to smelt iron by the ton: the Blast Furnace is unlocked.

name: Pig Iron
description: Coke iron makes boilers: Papin's digester becomes the Autoclave, and the mines go deeper.

name: Vulcanised Rubber
description: Goodyear's rubber: long chains are a material of their own. Polymerisation unlocked.

name: Hydrogen
description: Cavendish's inflammable air. The hunt for new elements begins in earnest.

name: Chlorine
description: Scheele's chlorine bleaches linen, and chemists start taking apart animal and vegetable matter.

name: Voltaic Pile
description: Volta's pile: electricity tears compounds apart. Electrolysis unlocked.

name: Iodine
description: Courtois's iodine came out of seaweed: plants hide elements, and medicines too. The apothecaries send their herbs.

name: Platinum
description: Platinum makes reactions go without being used up. Catalysis unlocked.

name: Dry Ice
description: Thilorier's dry ice at -78 C. The race to liquefy every gas has begun: the Air Liquefier is unlocked.

name: Benzene
description: Charles Mansfield fractionates coal tar into pure benzene (1849): the Fractionating Column is unlocked.

name: Urea
description: Wohler's urea: organic chemistry is just chemistry. The apothecary's shelf opens.

name: Quinine
description: Quinine from cinchona bark: chemists race to extract every plant's secret.

name: Dynamo
description: Siemens' dynamo makes electricity by the ton: the Electrolytic Cell is unlocked, and oil, bauxite and copper ore are worth digging.

name: Sodium bicarbonate
description: Solvay's ammonia soda (1861) founds the heavy chemical industry.

name: Fluorine
description: Henri Moissan isolated fluorine (1886); his electric arc furnace (1892) reaches 3,500 C. The Arc Furnace is unlocked.

name: Gasoline
description: Gasoline for the motor car. Catalytic crackers will make more of it from heavy oil: the Catalytic Cracker is unlocked.

name: Stainless Steel
description: Alloy steel strong enough to hold 200 atmospheres: the High-Pressure Reactor is unlocked.

name: Aspirin
description: Bayer's aspirin (1899): the pharmaceutical industry is born.

name: Bakelite
description: The age of plastics. Natural gas and rutile arrive.

name: Vanillin
description: Tiemann and Haarmann's synthetic vanilla (1874): the flavour industry learns to make what plants make.

name: Welsbach Gas Mantle
description: Welsbach's thorium mantle (1891) turns a gas flame into brilliant white light: the rare earths find their first use.

name: Monosodium glutamate
description: Kikunae Ikeda tastes kombu broth and names a fifth taste, umami (1908).

name: Dry Cell
description: Gassner's dry cell (1886): electricity you can carry in your pocket.

name: Tungsten Carbide
description: Moissan's carbides: in the arc furnace almost anything will combine with carbon, and the results are nearly as hard as diamond.

name: Polyethylene
description: ICI's polythene (1933), found by accident at 1,400 atmospheres. Meanwhile biochemists hunt the vitamins in bran, egg and spinach.

name: Nylon 6,6
description: Carothers' nylon (1935): 'as strong as steel, as fine as a spider's web'. Stockings sold out in a day in 1940.

name: Sulfanilamide
description: The sulfa drugs work, and Florey and Chain need penicillin by the vat: the Bioreactor is unlocked.

name: Vitamin C
description: Szent-Gyorgyi and Reichstein's vitamin C (1933): the hunt for every vitamin is on.

name: Cemented Carbide
description: Cemented carbide anvils hold 50,000 atmospheres: the Diamond Press is unlocked.

name: Polysilicon
description: Silicon pure to one part in a billion. Teal's Crystal Puller grows it into one flawless crystal.

name: Transistor
description: The transistor (1947). The silicon age opens: the CVD Chamber is unlocked.

name: Uranium
description: Uranium metal for Fermi's pile (Chicago, 2 December 1942): the Nuclear Reactor is unlocked.

name: Neptunium
description: Neptunium, the first element beyond uranium. Lawrence's cyclotron will reach further: the Cyclotron is unlocked.

name: Streptomycin
description: Streptomycin cures tuberculosis (1944): the golden age of antibiotics, dug out of the soil.

name: MOSFET
description: Atalla and Kahng's MOSFET (1959). Every chip ever since is built from it.

name: Microprocessor
description: The microprocessor (Intel 4004, 1971): 2,300 transistors on a chip. Today's carry tens of billions.

name: Blue LED
description: The blue LED (Akasaki, Amano, Nakamura, 1993; Nobel 2014). White light from a diode at last.

name: Human Insulin
description: Human insulin from bacteria (1978): biology becomes a factory.

name: Oganesson
description: Oganesson (Dubna, 2002; named 2016): the seventh row of the periodic table is complete.

name: A new era: Antiquity
description: Glass, soap, steel and spirits: the crafts of the ancient world.

name: A new era: Alchemy
description: The alchemists' acids dissolve almost anything, gold included.

name: A new era: Steam & Revolution
description: Coal, steam and the new elements: chemistry becomes a science.

name: A new era: Industry
description: Dynamos, furnaces and fertiliser: chemistry becomes an industry.

name: A new era: Modern
description: Plastics, antibiotics, the atom and the transistor.

name: A new era: Frontier
description: Chips, genes and materials built one atomic layer at a time.

name: Fully equipped
description: Unlock all 25 vessels.

name: The whole of chemistry
description: Discover all 1263 substances in the game.
